title: Routing: mirror sampled requests to shadow targets (fail-open + strict timeouts)
creator: Mina Haddad
project: Shadow traffic tool for eval metrics
description:
Implement data-plane support in Smart Routing to mirror (duplicate) a sampled subset of production inference requests to one or more configured shadow targets while always returning the control response to the caller.

Key requirements:
- Fail-open: user path must not depend on shadow path (no added error surface). Any shadow errors/timeouts must be swallowed and recorded as shadow outcomes only.
- Strict overhead budget: must not materially increase p99 latency for the control response; shadow dispatch must be async and bounded.
- Respect sampling + deterministic bucketing outputs from ENG-5403 (router gets a boolean decision + target list).
- Support multi-target shadowing (N shadow variants) with per-target timeout.
- Ensure mirrored requests do not consume user quotas / rate limits and do not block batching on control path.
- Streaming semantics are out of scope for MVP (tracked in ENG-5414); this ticket covers non-streaming chat/completions/embeddings mirroring.

Implementation is expected in the edge/router layer where we already have access to request metadata (tenant/route/model) and can fan-out without touching application response handling.
acceptance_criteria:
1) For eligible requests (per policy sampling/bucketing), router emits 1 control request and asynchronously emits mirrored shadow requests to configured shadow targets.
2) Control response latency impact: <1ms p50 increase and <5ms p99 increase at 5% sampling under synthetic load (see perf-canary suite results attached in PR).
3) Shadow requests are always best-effort: failures/timeouts never affect control response code/headers/body.
4) Shadow dispatch uses strict timeouts (connect + request) and hard bounds on concurrency/queueing to avoid resource exhaustion.
5) Per-target timeout + max bytes captured enforced; router does not buffer unbounded payloads.
6) Shadow requests carry shadow metadata headers (shadow_run_id / shadow_target_id / control_request_fingerprint) but do not forward end-user auth headers unless explicitly allowlisted by policy.
7) Unit + integration tests cover: sampling on/off, multi-target fanout, timeout path, shadow target 5xx, network failure, and ensure control path unaffected.
8) Logs/metrics include counters for shadow dispatched/succeeded/failed/timed_out and a gauge for shadow dispatch queue depth (cardinality-safe).
implementation_notes:
Approach (MVP): inline async mirroring from router with a dedicated shadow-dispatch executor.
- Router handles request normally (control). After request classification + fingerprinting, it enqueues one task per shadow target to a bounded executor.
- Executor uses a separate HTTP client pool configured with: shorter connect timeout, shorter overall timeout, lower max in-flight per host, and no retries by default (retries increase tail and cost).
- Shadow payload is constructed from the canonicalized request (post validation) with redaction hooks (headers/body allowlist) and shadow metadata headers.
- Result handling: we record minimal outcome (success/failure/timeout, status code class, latency bucket, response size) and pass payload references to telemetry ingestion (full schema work in ENG-5404).
- Cancellation: if executor queue is full, drop shadow task and increment dropped counter (still considered fail-open).

Not included:
- Streaming mirroring (ENG-5414)
- Circuit breaker/backpressure policy knobs beyond a fixed queue bound (follow-up ENG-5415)
- Persisting full prompt/response artifacts (handled downstream by telemetry + retention/redaction pipeline)
progress_updates: 2025-12-06: Implemented basic fanout skeleton behind feature flag shadow_mirror_enabled; wired to policy decision stub. Added counters for dispatched/failed.
2025-12-12: Added bounded executor + queue depth gauge; implemented per-target timeout and connect timeout separation. Updated unit tests to cover queue-full drop behavior.
2025-12-18: Integrated deterministic fingerprint from ENG-5403 branch; ensured same fingerprint used for control+shadow and passed via headers.
2026-01-03: Ran perf-canary shadow mirror benchmark at 1%/5% sampling; observed +0.6ms p50 / +3.8ms p99 at 5% in worst-case config. Tightened client pool limits to reduce CPU spikes.
2026-01-09: Addressed SRE review: ensured no retries, no shared connection pool with control path, and added guard to never propagate shadow failures to user response.
2026-01-14: Merged and enabled for internal dogfood tenant (behind feature flag + allowlist).
